title: Bolivia vs Jordan: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: For most travelers seeking rugged adventure on a lean budget, Bolivia is the clear choice. It delivers raw, high-altitude experiences and distinct cultural immersion at a fraction of Jordan's cost. faq.question: What are the main altitude considerations for Bolivia?
faq.answer: Bolivia has many high-altitude areas like La Paz (3,640m) and Potosí (4,090m). Travelers often experience altitude sickness. It is recommended to spend at least 2-3 days acclimatizing upon arrival, drink plenty of water, and avoid strenuous activity immediately. Coca leaves or pills can help manage symptoms.

faq.question: Is the Jordan Pass worth it for visitors?
faq.answer: Yes, for most visitors staying 3 nights or more, the Jordan Pass is highly recommended. It includes entry to over 40 attractions, including Petra, Jerash, and Wadi Rum, and waives the visa fee (40 JOD/$56 USD) for eligible nationalities. A 1-day Petra pass plus visa already exceeds the pass cost of 70-80 JOD ($99-113 USD).

faq.question: How safe is solo female travel in Bolivia versus Jordan?
faq.answer: Jordan is generally considered safer for solo female travelers, with a lower crime rate and a welcoming culture. Modest dress is advised. Bolivia requires more vigilance due to higher petty crime rates and less developed infrastructure. Basic Spanish skills are more critical in Bolivia for solo navigation.

faq.question: What is the best way to get from Amman to Petra?
faq.answer: The most common and reliable way is via JETT bus, which costs about 10-15 JOD ($14-21 USD) and takes approximately 3-4 hours. Alternatively, you can rent a car for flexibility or hire a private taxi, which will be significantly more expensive (around 70-90 JOD/$99-127 USD one-way).

faq.question: Can I visit the Amazon rainforest from Bolivia?
faq.answer: Yes, you can. Rurrenabaque in northern Bolivia is a gateway to both the Madidi National Park (jungle tours) and the Beni Biological Station (pampas tours). Multi-day tours typically last 3-4 days and cost 1200-2000 BOB ($175-290 USD), offering opportunities to see capybaras, monkeys, and caimans.

faq.question: What are the visa requirements for US citizens for both countries?
faq.answer: For Bolivia, US citizens can obtain a visa on arrival at major entry points for approximately $160 USD, valid for 90 days. For Jordan, US citizens can obtain a visa on arrival for 40 JOD ($56 USD) or purchase the Jordan Pass in advance, which includes the visa fee if staying at least 3 nights.

faq.question: How much Spanish is needed for Bolivia?
faq.answer: Basic conversational Spanish is highly recommended for travel in Bolivia. While some tour operators and hotels in major tourist hubs may have English-speaking staff, outside these areas, English is rarely spoken. Knowing phrases for directions, ordering food, and bus tickets will greatly enhance your experience.

faq.question: What are the driving conditions like in Jordan?
faq.answer: Driving in Jordan is generally straightforward with good road conditions, especially on major routes connecting cities and tourist sites. Signage is often in both Arabic and English. Driving in Amman can be chaotic, but outside the capital, it is relatively calm. A 4x4 is not necessary unless venturing off-road in specific desert areas.
